trust_decision.summary: Before plugin load hooks read a file for a dev-server request, isServerAccessDeniedForTransform decides whether the id falls under server.fs, but only for ids that carry a query on its allow-list (raw/url/inline/.svg). ?vite-wasm-instance was not on that list, so the wasm load hook read files outside the allow-list. The WebAssembly.compile error, which includes the file's first bytes, then reached the client through the error overlay.

landing_point.why: The summary names `?vite-wasm-instance`. That string appears only in the wasm plugin, where isInstance makes the hook skip the `.wasm` path requirement and call parseWasm on any file. The real fix lives in a different module, the transform-middleware allow-list.

fix_sites.entry_point: Dev-server HTTP GET for any module URL with ?vite-wasm-instance (e.g. /path?import&vite-wasm-instance or /@fs/abs/path?vite-wasm-instance), handled by viteTransformMiddleware -> environment.transformRequest -> loadAndTransform
fix_sites.module_kind: server middleware access-check helper (core); the fix site at fix.diff:217-230 is the same line in a backport commit

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches one line in transform.ts. Its sink (parseWasm) is in plugins/wasm.ts, but the fix did not change that file.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the direct `.wasm` route (O8), a solver could argue the advisory is about the `?vite-wasm-instance` query, and that a plain `.wasm` URL with no query is the normal ESM-integration import path that only exposes import/export names of a real wasm binary, so it is not the reported leak.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Importing a wasm module that exports a WebAssembly.Global must keep working. The generated wrapper glue and the wasm-to-wasm global imports both import `<file>.wasm?vite-wasm-instance` in their own code, so blocking or stripping the query outright breaks legitimate wasm global imports inside the allow-list.

O6_input_shapes: regex anchored with (?:&|$) so it matches the plugin's own wasmInstanceRE exactly (fix.diff:217; packages/vite/src/node/plugins/wasm.ts:21)

O7_producer.where: packages/vite/src/node/plugins/wasm.ts:241-267 (parseWasm puts the compile error message, which carries the leading bytes, into a thrown Error), serialised to the client by packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/error.ts:11-23

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A direct `.wasm` id with no query (e.g. /@fs/<outside>/x.wasm?import, with ?import stripped) matches wasmDirectRE, so parseWasm reads the file. The allow-list check returns false because no listed query is present, which exposes import/export names or, for a non-wasm file named *.wasm, the leading-byte compile error, outside server.fs.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Plain `.wasm` imports are the normal WASM ESM-integration path and the advisory names only the query, so the route looks like intended behaviour.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same file as the landing point (wasm.ts), but the gate lives in server/middlewares/transform.ts:64

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another internal query (like ?inline) that makes fileToDevUrl read file bytes, which the transform.ts allow-list would also have to list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The allow-list in transform.ts is a hand-kept regex list with a TODO to consolidate it with the plugin regexes (packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/transform.ts:54). Each new plugin query that reads files has to be added by hand, which is exactly how this bug arose.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second internal wasm layer suffix (for example a table/memory instance layer) that also bypasses the `.wasm`-suffix requirement.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The instance layer was itself added as an internal suffix for WebAssembly.Global. A sibling layer for other export kinds would be a natural extension.

O9_family: Path/access-control bypass leading to information exposure via error message (server.fs allow-list query bypass; CWE-22/200/209)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + pnpm monorepo; vite package built with rolldown; tests via vitest and playwright playground tests
O10_build.project_tests: playground/fs-serve (__tests__/commonTests.ts matrix driven by root/src/index.html and root/matrixTestResultPlugin.ts); the wasm playground covers legitimate wasm/global imports

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: In wasm.ts, require cleanUrl(id) to end in `.wasm` for the instance layer, or hide the compile error text. Either blocks .env but still reads (and exposes names of) `.wasm` files outside server.fs, and never touches the allow-list gate.

out_of_scope_notes: forwardConsole.ts:138 reads a stack file for a code frame that goes to the server terminal; not this advisory's route.

The pinned tree already has fs-serve matrix tests for other wasm?init query bypasses (playground/fs-serve/root/src/index.html:122-125, 151-154), so this area has a history of repeated query-allow-list bypasses.
unverified: The O8 direct-.wasm route is inferred from reading wasm.ts:13/138-139 and transform.ts:64; I did not trace whether resolve or any other middleware rejects /@fs/ paths outside allow before load. present_in_latest is unknown because no latest release is available.

Bundled-dev mode (fileToBuiltUrl reads the file at packages/vite/src/node/plugins/asset.ts:459) was not checked against this gate; the fix's test matrix runs under !isBundledDev in one backport (fix.diff:238).
